name: Герои Эхо недели аппаратов — пастухи горных островов, отбившие нашествие Медного Архая «Шествие медных» (ADR-0023, ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Аппараты — Медный Архай»; RS.weeks в design/ui/roster.js). Пятеро по герою за цикл II–VI: c2-49 Лаон Семь Кож, c3-53 Ариэна Нить Лабиринта, c4-54 Эвмел Масло Ран, c5-60 Пиррос Молот Пяты, c6-54 Кересса Жар Недр. Задание 30.09.2026: портреты для окон призыва и Эхо вместо инициалов. Рецепт — принятый отряд Иш-Кантуна (jobs/heroes-echo-ishkantun.json) и способ «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md); в рамке — нижний край режет фигуру по поясу и внизу ничего не написано. Раса — Забытые, облик ни на кого из нынешних не похож. Пастухи островов — решение агента по главам: крепкие, короткошеие, квадратная челюсть, очень большие глаза бледно-морского цвета, загар с солёным налётом, чёрные тугие кудри на шерстяной ленте; козья шерсть, овчина, глина, бронза; масло из горьких ягод. Враги недели — медные машины Архая, огненные быки, медные великаны, лабиринты (jobs/echo-copperarchai.json) — только трофеи и угроза за правым краем. Класс — по оружию и действию, школа — по цвету света. Детали, которых нет в «кто он» и главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no Greek letters, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. The hero is flesh and blood, not a machine: no copper plates, no rivets and no gears on the hero's body; no crested helmet.

heroes.frame:
Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the belt or the hips; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame, whatever the pose. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there, but nothing is written there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the shepherds of the mountain islands — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, on steep rocky islands in a dark sea, grazing goats on terraced pastures and pressing oil from bitter berries. They look unlike any people living now: compact and strong, with broad shoulders, short thick necks, square jaws, straight heavy brows and very large eyes of pale sea-green; their skin is deeply sun-browned with a salty, weathered sheen; their hair is black and grows in dense tight curls, worn long and tied back with strips of undyed wool. They wear cloaks of coarse goat hair and sheepskin, short kilts and wraps of undyed wool, leather straps, simple bronze and bone; their tools are shepherd's crooks, slings, clay oil jars, bronze and stone. Their enemies were the guardians of Copper Archai — machines of hammered copper and bronze plates held by big rivets, with fire burning inside them instead of blood and glowing through the seams, their faces calm copper masks with almond eyes; fire-breathing copper bulls, copper giants that walked the shore three times a day, and builders who turned the valleys into labyrinths of pale stone; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

jobs.subject: Subject: Laon Seven-Hides, a man of the mountain islands, a shepherd and defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the copper guards walked the shore three times a day for as long as the grandfathers remembered, and his people lived by their step. One day the first round did not come to the shore: the copper ones climbed up to the pastures — huge, green with age, creaking at every knee. His shield was made of seven bull hides sewn one on top of another, and every blow cost him a hide; six he gave before noon, while his people drove the goats into the mountains. Right now a copper guard strikes again. Character: stubborn, stoic and full of cold hatred for the even, merciless rhythm of the machines; his jaw clenched, his heavy brows lowered, his pale sea-green eyes fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge. Pose, the moment of the blow: the camera is low; he stands on a stony pasture, turned toward the right, his shoulders driven forward into the shield. He has exactly two arms: his near arm drives a tall oval shield of seven layered bull hides forward toward the right as a huge copper fist slams into it from the right edge — the outer hides are torn through and hang in flaps; his far hand grips a long shepherd's crook of dark wood held low behind the shield. Amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from the stony ground under the blow; pebbles and dust leap. Details that tell his story: (1) the torn layers of hide peel back in flaps, only one or two left whole; (2) green smears of verdigris on the shield where the copper struck; (3) a bronze goat bell hangs at his belt; (4) a heavy cloak of black goat hair over one shoulder; (5) far behind him, goats flee up the mountain paths. Place: a high goat pasture on a rocky island at night, low walls of piled stone, the dark sea far below with the silhouette of a copper giant on the shore. Amber light rises from the cracks in the rock below; cold teal sea-light from behind.

jobs.subject: Subject: Ariena Thread-of-the-Labyrinth, a woman of the mountain islands, a controller of the Air school. Who she is: the copper builders put up walls without windows or doors, and in one round a valley became a labyrinth where only they could walk, by count. She had grazed goats in those valleys since childhood and knew them better than the walls. She left the end of her yarn at the exit, took the thread between her teeth — her hands were needed to touch the walls — and went in, leading the copper ones into dead ends of their own labyrinths, where they stood marching on the spot until they cooled. Right now a copper guard follows her into a turn of the labyrinth. Character: daring, cool and quick-witted — a goatherd who fears nothing she can outthink; her eyes bright and alert, the corners of her mouth lifted around the thread. Pose, the moment of the lure: the camera is low; she stands at a sharp turn of a narrow stone corridor, turned toward the right, where the copper guard approaches. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is raised toward the right, two fingers beckoning the machine on, and a spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school curls from her fingers down the corridor, pulling the enemy after her; her far palm is pressed flat against the pale stone wall, feeling the way. A single red woollen thread is held between her teeth and runs back taut over her shoulder into the darkness behind her. Details that tell her story: (1) the red thread between her teeth, stretched taut; (2) a ball of red yarn, half unwound, at her belt; (3) her fingertips are worn from sliding along the walls; (4) a goatherd's sling and a small bronze bell at her hip; (5) the walls around her are high and blank, of pale stone, with no windows and no doors. Place: deep inside a labyrinth of pale stone at night: narrow corridors, a strip of starry sky high above, the orange glow of fire from the seams of a copper guard reflected on the wall at the right. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the cracks in the stone floor below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Evmel Oil-of-Wounds, a man of the mountain islands, a healer of the Water school. Who he is: on his island oil is pressed from bitter berries, and it heals everything that burns; he kept it in jars buried in the earth so that it would not warm. When the fire-breathing copper bulls came, the burns went down to the bone, and he mixed the oil with sea water, as the grandfathers did; when a bull came out of the labyrinth straight at the boats where the wounded lay, he stood between them. Right now he heals the wounded in the boats at the edge of the sea. Character: calm, gentle and brave — a healer who stays where he is needed; his face serious and kind, his brows lifted in concentration, his eyes on the wound. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; he stands waist-deep in the dark sea beside a boat, turned toward the right, leaning forward. He has exactly two arms: his near arm tilts a clay jar, and a stream of golden oil mixed with glowing blue sea water pours toward the right onto the burned beyond the right edge; his far hand scoops up sea water in his palm, and blue light of the Water school rises from it. Details that tell his story: (1) the clay jar is still crusted with earth from being buried; (2) his hands and forearms shine with oil; (3) an old burn in the shape of a palm on his shoulder — the mark of hot copper; (4) a sponge and cloths hang from a cord across his chest; (5) his black curls are tied back with a strip of wool, wet with spray. Place: the shore of the island at night: boats pulled up on the pebbles, the dark sea, and far behind, the red glow of fire from a copper bull at the mouth of the labyrinth. Blue light of the Water school rises from the sea around him.

jobs.subject: Subject: Pirros Heel-Hammer, a man of the mountain islands, a smith and a warrior of great strength of the Fire school. Who he is: his forge stood above the shore, and three times a day a copper guard walked past it. As a boy he picked up a drop that fell from a giant — thick and glowing, like living copper — and it burned his palm until evening; since then he looked at the copper ones like a smith: where the seams are, where the rivets are, where it flows from. On the right heel of the greatest giant he saw a rivet that shone differently — a new one; where it was repaired, it is weak. He forged a short heavy hammer with a beak for that one rivet. Right now he strikes the heel of the giant. Character: grim, focused and relentless — a smith's patience turned into fury; his teeth clenched, his heavy brows drawn down, his eyes locked on the rivet. Pose, the moment of the blow: the camera is low; he lunges up and toward the right beneath a colossal copper heel that fills the right edge of the picture, raised for a step. He has exactly two arms: both hands swing a short, heavy hammer with a beaked head upward into the gleaming new rivet of the heel; the rivet flies out, and a jet of molten fire bursts from the heel like wine from a pierced skin, pouring down in streams (Fire). Scarlet-orange light of the Fire school floods him from the wound in the heel. Details that tell his story: (1) the hammer is short and heavy, with a beak like a bird's; (2) a round old burn scar in the middle of his palm; (3) a smith's leather apron, scorched and holed; (4) the sand around him is turning to glass where the fire falls; (5) tongs and a rivet punch hang from his belt. Place: the shore of the island at night, the enormous copper leg of a giant covered in verdigris and rivets, the dark sea beyond. Scarlet fire pours down from the upper right; the sea glows teal behind.

jobs.subject: Subject: Keressa Heat-of-the-Deep, a woman of the mountain islands, a battle mage of the Fire school. Who she is: her island stood on a mountain, and the mountain stood on fire: if you put your ear to a crack you could hear the heat breathing. She could call that heat up, a handful at a time — to warm a house or temper a blade. She learned that the heat of the deep goes to whoever is colder, and that she could call out even the old fire that burned inside the copper ones; when she called up the heat of the whole mountain, the fire in every copper one heard it and went to it, and they stopped where they stood. Right now she pulls the fire out of a copper guard. Character: proud, fierce and pitiless toward the machines — there is nothing in them to pity, only fire and count; her head high, her eyes burning with reflected fire, her lips parted in a command. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands on the slope of the mountain, turned toward the right, leaning back as she pulls. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is thrust out toward the right with the fingers curled like claws, and she draws toward her long ribbons of molten fire streaming out of the seams of a copper guard beyond the right edge, spiralling into her palm; her far hand is pressed flat against a glowing crack in the rock beside her. Scarlet-orange light of the Fire school blazes between her hands. Details that tell her story: (1) her palms shine with healing oil and glow red from within; (2) the end of a red woollen thread is tied around her wrist — the thread of a friend who did not come out of the labyrinth; (3) soot on her ear and cheek from pressing them to the cracks; (4) her black curls are tied up with a strip of wool, a few loose and lifted by the heat; (5) a heavy cloak of goat hair thrown back from her shoulders. Place: the slope of a fire mountain on the island at night: cracks in the rock glowing red, a stone house below, the labyrinth and the dark sea far away. Scarlet light rises from the cracks in the rock below; teal sea-light rims her from behind.
